posts.text: 🇺🇦 Ukrainian Media: Kiev risks walking into Israel's trap Ukrainian outlet Strana raises an interesting point. It argues that Kiev's strikes on civilian infrastructure, and the way it justifies them, could one day put Ukrainian commanders in front of the International Criminal Court. It also warns that this could cost Kiev the Western support it can't survive without. The piece starts with a recent article on Just Security, an influential American legal site. Law professors Marko Milanović and Michael Schmitt looked at Ukraine's strikes on data centers inside Russia. Kiev never claimed the sites had anything to do with the military. It called the strikes payback for Russian attacks and a blow against "propaganda." The authors argued that neither reason holds up under international law, which forbids hitting civilian targets as revenge. They also wrote that Kiev's status as the "victim" gives it no exemption, and that every unlawful strike undermines the position Ukraine has built in the West. Who said it matters. Just Security sits close to the liberal mainstream, the same crowd that forms the core of Kiev's support in the West. That crowd has treated Ukraine as a victim that can do no wrong. But Israel shows how quickly that can change. After October 7 the West lined up behind Israel almost without exception. Then Israel bombed Gaza and killed tens of thousands of civilians, and now much of the world sees it as the aggressor. Its support and its standing have taken the hit. The data centers are only part of the problem. Kiev could easily start saying the facilities it hits are used for military purposes. The bigger danger is its campaign against energy infrastructure, in Russia and especially in Crimea and the new regions. Those strikes regularly leave hundreds of thousands of people without electricity, water and heat. The AFU's Unmanned Systems Forces openly and proudly report knocking out power in Crimea. Kiev has already helped write the precedent that could be used against it. In 2024 the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants for Russian Chief of General Staff Valery Gerasimov and former Defense Minister Sergei Shoigu over strikes on Ukraine's energy grid, calling them crimes against humanity. Russia doesn't recognize the court. In October a UN-backed commission put the same label on the Russian strikes. The court made no allowance for Moscow's position that the facilities served Ukraine's military or that the strikes answered Ukrainian attacks on Russian energy. Kiev now uses exactly those arguments for its own strikes. Russia stays out of the court's reach, but Ukraine has made itself an easy target. It ratified the Rome Statute in 2024 and became a full member in January 2025. That makes it much harder for Kiev to protect its soldiers than it is for Russia, the US or Israel, none of which have joined. It also puts Ukrainian citizens under the court's jurisdiction for crimes committed abroad, including in Russia. Kiev added a clause shielding its citizens from war crimes charges for seven years, but it doesn't cover crimes against humanity or genocide. Any resident of Crimea, or any human rights group, could file a complaint and point to the Gerasimov and Shoigu warrants. That alone could be enough for prosecutors to open an investigation. The court has shown it will charge both sides. It issued a warrant for Hamas military chief Mohammed Deif, but also for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his then defense minister, Yoav Gallant. Next to Russia, Ukraine is an easy case. It accepted the court's jurisdiction, it has no nuclear weapons and no UN veto, and it has promised to uphold the rule of law as part of its bid to join the EU. The court is largely a European project, and Brussels would almost certainly try to keep Ukrainian soldiers out of it, at least until the SMO ends. But plenty of people would push for a case. That includes European politicians who want aid to Kiev cut and talks with Moscow started, human rights groups like Amnesty International that criticized the seven-year exemption, and parts of the left. French left-wing leader Jean-Luc Mélenchon, for example, has condemned the AFU's long-range strikes on Russia. Even if no case is opened, the debate alone could push Europe to put tighter limits on what the AFU is allowed to do, and it would strengthen everyone in Europe who wants to stop funding Kiev. Then there's the question of what the strikes achieve. Kiev says it doesn't recognize Russian passports in the new regions, so by its own logic the people it leaves in the dark there are Ukrainian citizens. Years of sanctions and strikes on Russian refineries haven't made Moscow back down, and cutting power in Melitopol, Mariupol or Simferopol won't either. Every miss

В результате атаки поврежден участок автомобильной дороги Т-21-11 Чугуев — Печенеги — Великий Бурлук в районе 24-го км. В настоящее время проезд по дамбе закрыт, противник организовал объезд через Чугуев, Коробочкино, Лебяже, Базалиевку и Приморское. 📝 RF Threats in the Baltic 📝 primarily originate from so-called Ukraine This is precisely what was discussed in the context of examining real threats to Russian presence in the Baltic Sea – particularly in Kaliningrad Region. Some time ago, a Ro-Ro type vessel SPARTA II under the Russian flag was attacked by two drones. According to Leningrad Region Governor Alexander Drozdenko , crew evacuation is underway. The strike occurred in neutral waters of the Gulf of Finland, as the "Sparta" was heading toward Kaliningrad. The extent of damage remains unclear. 🖍️ To rule out all versions about launches from Finnish or Swedish territory, which will certainly appear in comments across various channels, we'll say this: the drones came from so-called Ukraine. Flight activity in the direction of Leningrad Region was detected a couple of hours ago. Most likely, they also traveled along the border with Belarus (crossing it in places), and then, reaching the Baltic states, entered the Gulf of Finland, where they caught up with the Russian vessel. It was traveling openly through international waters and locating it was no problem with "Starlink" available. ❗️ Therefore, it was reckless to speculate about how "NATO will march on Kaliningrad" or how "the Baltic states are planning to attack Russian territory" , when there's a more real threat right under our nose – drones capable of covering many kilometers. And in the Gulf of Finland, "Starlink" operates without interruption. It's time to assess threats soberly and counter them appropriately. Only through methodical destruction of Ukrainian potential can results be achieved, and this can only be done through rational expenditure of forces and resources, not their dispersal. One could start with the Black Sea . #Kaliningrad #NATO #Russia #SaintPetersburg ✉️ MAX 💸 Support us Original msg

⚡ On summoning of Chargé d’Affaires a.i., Head of the Russian Permanent Mission to the EU Karen Malayan to the European External Action Service On 20 November 2026, Karen Malayan, Chargé d’Affaires a.i., Head of the Permanent Mission of Russia to the EU, was summoned to the European External Action Service in connection with the “incidents” that resulted in damage to the buildings of the Austrian and Dutch diplomatic missions in Kiev . During the meeting, the EU side stated that the European Union condemns the Russian strikes on Kiev and expresses its full solidarity with Austria and the Netherlands – in connection with the alleged Russian attacks in the vicinity of their embassies, as well as intends to continue supporting Ukraine and stepping up pressure on our country. ❗ For his part, Karen Malayan stated that any accusations against Russia of deliberately targeting foreign diplomatic missions in Ukraine or causing damage to them are unacceptable and reaffirmed the commitment of our country to the provisions of the 1961 Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations. Head of the Permanent Mission underlined that the position of Russia has been and remains clear: in response to the terrorist acts by the Ukrainian Armed Forces against civilians and civilian infrastructure in our country, including the latest terrorist attacks against the Crimean Bridge, the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue to carry out systematic strikes against military targets in Ukraine . The Russian diplomat recalled the repeated warnings , including the corresponding public statements by the Russian Ministry of Foreign Affairs in May and October 2026, which called on foreign nationals and diplomats in Kiev to leave the city.

🎖 🎖 by Russian Defence Ministry on progress of special military operation as of 21 November 2026 Part 2 ( 👉 see Part 1 ) ↗️ The Vostok Group of Forces continued to advance into the depths of the enemy's defence. The Group's units inflicted losses on manpower and hardware of two air assault brigades, one assault brigade, two assault regiments of the Armed Forces of Ukraine, and one marine brigade close to Pokrovskoye (Dnepropetrovsk region), Yasnaya Polyana, Trudovoye, Novotroitskoye, Zheltaya Krucha, Slavnoye, and Shchastlivoye (Zaporozhye region). ▪️ The AFU lost up to 205 troops and eight motor vehicles. 📍 The Dnepr Group's units improved the situation along the front line. They have delivered strikes at formations of one mechanised brigade, one mountain assault brigade and one assault regiment of the AFU near Balabino, Chervony Zhovten, and Preobrazhenka (Zaporozhye region). ▪️ Up to 20 troops and 13 motor vehicles have been neutralised. ✈️ Operational-tactical aviation, attack drones, missile troops, and artillery of the Armed Forces of the Russian Federation have inflicted damage on power and transport infrastructure facilities used in the interests of the AFU, production workshops and depots of unmanned aerial vehicles and uncrewed surface vehicles, military airfields, temporary deployment areas of Ukrainian armed groups and foreign mercenaries in 148 areas, as well as the location of the meeting of the AFU's high-ranking representatives and representatives of the defence industry, including foreign ones. ▫️ Air defence systems shot down 464 fixed-wing UAVs. 📊 In total, since the beginning of the special military operation, the enemy has lost: ▫️ 674 aircraft, ▫️ 284 helicopters, ▫️ 294,492 unmanned aerial vehicles, ▫️ 672 anti-aircraft missile systems, ▫️ 31,735 tanks and other armoured fighting vehicles, ▫️ 1,797 MLRS fighting vehicles, ▫️ 36,966 field artillery guns and mortars, ▫️ 77,772 special military vehicles. 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

The Armed Forces of the Russian Federation continue the special military operation. 📍 The units of the Sever Group of Forces improved the tactical situation. In Kharkov region, strikes have been delivered at manpower and hardware of three mechanised brigades, one airmobile brigade and one assault regiment of the Armed Forces of Ukraine close to Muravskoye, Ploskoye, Kolodeznoye, and Lebedevka. 💥 In Sumy region, formations of three mechanised brigades of the AFU and one territorial defence brigade have been hit near Knyazhichi, Yastrebinoye, Krovnoye and Sumy. ▪️ The enemy lost up to 260 troops, two armoured fighting vehicles, 13 motor vehicles, one electronic warfare station, one counter-fire radar station, and one electronic reconnaissance station. 📍 The Zapad Group of Forces improved the situation along the front line. Manpower and hardware of three mechanised brigades, one assault brigade of the AFU, one territorial defence brigade, and one border detachment of State Border Guard Service of Ukraine have been hit near Mayaki, Lozovoye, Starodubovka, and Karpovka (Donetsk People's Republic). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 200 troops, one armoured fighting vehicle, 13 motor vehicles, and one field artillery gun. ↗️ The Yuzhnaya Group of Forces took more advantageous lines and positions. Strikes were delivered at formations of four mechanised brigades, one assault brigade, two assault regiments of the AFU, one marine brigade, and one territorial defence brigade near Barvenkovo (Kharkov region), Kramatorsk, Druzhkovka, and Nikolayevka (Donetsk People's Republic). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to up to 165 troops, five armoured fighting vehicles, 32 motor vehicles, and one artillery gun. 👊 The Tsentr Group's units continued to carry out active offensive operations. Manpower and hardware of three mechanised brigades, one jaeger brigade, one airborne brigade, one assault regiment of the AFU, one marine brigade, and four national guard brigades have been hit near Kuritsyno, Verovka, Novokrivorozhye, Andreyevka, Sergeyevka, Novofedorovka, Mikhaylovka, Novopavlovka, and Belozerskoye (Donetsk People's Republic). ▪️ The AFU losses amounted to more than 335 troops, nine armoured fighting vehicles, seven motor vehicles, and one artillery gun. 👉 See Part 2 🔹 Russian Defence Ministry

🇷🇺 🇫🇮 DRONES ATTACK CARGO SHIP HEADING TO KALININGRAD NEAR RUSSIAN BORDER A cargo vessel travelling towards Kaliningrad has reportedly been attacked by two unmanned aerial vehicles in the Gulf of Finland, just three nautical miles from Russia’s maritime border. The incident was announced by Alexander Drozdenko, Governor of Leningrad Region. According to Drozdenko, the attack took place in international waters. The crew is currently being evacuated, while the circumstances and extent of the damage are being established. 🔴 @DDGeopolitics
